title: Effects of fish meal replacement with blended protein sources in an extruded pellet diet on growth and digestibility of the olive flounder (Paralichthys olivaceus)
content:
Abstract

The present study investigated the effect of substituting fish meal (FM) with alternative blended protein sources (BPS; i.e., wheat gluten, soy protein concentrate, tankage meal, tuna by-product meal, and poultry by-product meal), supplemented with essential amino acids (EAAs), in the diet of the olive flounder (Paralichthys olivaceus). The experimental diet was prepared as a commercial reference diet (CRD) for the control (Con) group, with 50% of FM replaced by BPS for the low-FM (LF) diet group. Following a 60-day feeding period, no significant differences were observed in flounder growth performance or the chemical composition of the gastric contents. However, there were significant differences in the chemical composition of crude protein and crude lipids in dorsal muscle. For the LF group, activity levels of the digestive enzyme amylase were significantly higher in the middle intestine, but no difference was observed in the stomach. Lipase activity was higher in both the stomach and middle intestine in the LF group. Trypsin activity in the middle intestine was higher in the LF group, but the opposite trend was observed for the stomach. In conclusion, substituting 50% FM with BPS supplemented with EAAs had no adverse effect on the growth of P. olivaceus.
